label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Hello D. Bergeron, Hélène here, from Le Pétrin Doré. You are right that people deserve a straight answer, especially when they have paid for bread in advance. So let me give you one before this goes any further: **we are not closing or moving. I bought the building.** The bakery is staying, and so are the people who live upstairs.

I had hoped to keep this as a surprise for the reopening. Clearly, that was not my best idea! What was meant to be happy news has worried people instead, and I am sorry for that. Looking at the sign now, with no explanation beside it, I understand why people started asking questions.

First, the carnets, because I do not want anyone left wondering about their money. We sold 214 bread carnets in October, at $60 for 12 loaves. **Every one of them is still valid, with no expiry date.** If you have seven loaves left, you still have seven loaves waiting for you. Nothing about the sale of the building or our January work changes that.

Every carnet holder can also have a free croissant in January, with my thanks for your patience. And if anyone would rather have their money back, please come and see me at the bakery. I will refund you, no questions asked. You do not have to explain yourself or feel uncomfortable asking.

I do want to say something about the word “scam.” I have been on this corner since March 2009. I know many of you, your children, your usual bread orders, and sometimes whether you are having a good morning before you say a word. Reading that someone thought I might take your money and disappear hurt me. But I understand that a vague sign is not an answer, and knowing me is not a substitute for explaining what is happening. So I hope this clears it up: your carnets will be honoured, and refunds are available if that is what you prefer.

Now, the happy part.

Marc-Antoine, your cousin was half right: the building was sold. But it was sold to me! We signed at the notary on December 15.

M. Ferland is 81 and is retiring to Sherbrooke to be near his daughter. Before offering the building to anybody else, he offered me the chance to buy it. This is a very big thing for a small bakery owner, and it is still a little hard for me to believe that it has happened.

He has come in every morning for his baguette “pas trop cuite” for 17 years. At the notary, he cried a little. It was an emotional day. I wanted to tell you all when the work was finished and I could open the door and show you what we had done. Instead, I am telling you here, which is perhaps less pretty, but much better than letting everyone worry.

To our upstairs tenants, and to the neighbours worried about them: **the three apartments are staying rented, with the same tenants and the same rent.** I have promised them this in writing. There is no plan to turn their homes into condos. They should not have to read rumours on a neighbourhood board and wonder what is happening to their homes.

The bakery will be closed **January 4 through January 18 for work. We reopen Tuesday, January 19, at 7 a.m.**

We are getting a new four-deck oven from a supplier in Laval. Our old oven dates from 1998 and has broken down three times this year. Those of you who have arrived to find me looking very unhappy beside it will understand why I am looking forward to the new one. It has done a lot of work, but I think we have asked enough of it now.

We are also taking the space at the back, the old dépanneur storage area, and making room for six small tables. Finally, you will be able to sit down! It will still be our little bakery, just with a better oven and somewhere to have your coffee without standing in the doorway.

About the half-empty shelves on the 28th: that was not a sign that we were winding down. We had sold through our Christmas baking. We made 400 bûches for Christmas Eve, and the shelves were looking rather tired afterwards. So were we. It had nothing to do with closing the business.

And the famous sign: my nephew Thomas wrote it at six in the morning. “Grande nouvelle” was his idea, and I said yes without thinking much further than that. Please do not blame him. I am the owner, and I approved it. We thought we were giving people something nice to look forward to. We did not think about how it might look beside empty shelves, or what people might hear about the building being sold. I should have simply written, “Closed for renovations. Back January 19. We are staying!”

I do understand the worry. Mile End has lost too many small shops, and people have good reasons to be nervous when another window gets a mysterious notice. I love this neighbourhood too. Buying the building is my way of making a future for the bakery here, not preparing to leave it.

Priya, thank you for your kind words, and thank you to everyone who defended us or gave us the benefit of the doubt. It meant a great deal to read those messages. Thank you also to the people who asked what was happening. I would rather answer you directly than have you walking past and thinking we were gone.

Although we will be back baking on Tuesday the 19th, **please all come on Saturday, January 23, to celebrate with us.** We will have free coffee and a piece of the new bread for everyone. Come see the oven, try a seat at one of our six tables, and say hello. You are welcome whether you defended us, worried about us, or just found this thread and now want some bread.

So that is the news: same bakery, same address, a new oven, a few tables, and an owner who should have written a clearer sign.

Thank you for caring about our little place. I look forward to seeing you.

Hélène  
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré  
5 rue Fairmount
